tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

ballin-setup-frame-589-municipalities: Section 5, p.14: 589 municipalities of one region (REG = 1); twenty non-empty atomic strata, four singletons (Table 1 shows four zero-SD rows)
ballin-setup-cv-five-percent-k4: Section 5, p.14: the CV of five percent per target variable and K = 4 are stated as the setup
ballin-scope-case-study-not-controlled: Abstract and Section 1: the authors say the solvers differ in hardware, budget, iterations and, for IBM, the encoding, so the work is a case study. Table 2 in Section 5.1 backs it
ballin-scope-twenty-strata-free-tier-ope: Section 5.1, p.14: the authors state why the frame has twenty strata. Note the same section says the Dirac-3 boundary at L = 25 was not tested, so 'largest problem' is their stated rationale, not a measured limit
ballin-ibm-no-simulator-check-no-energy-: Section 6.1, p.17: the authors state that no check against an ideal or lightly-noised simulator was done, and that the evidence of failed optimisation is the lack of energy improvement over two iterations and a diffuse bitstring distribution
ballin-ibm-run-details-p-and-shots-not-r: Appendix A.5, p.24: ibm_kingston (Heron r2, 156 qubits) is named; p and shots per evaluation are stated as not recorded in a reportable form
ballin-ibm-binary-label-encoding-40-qubi: Section 4.6, p.10: IBM uses b = ceil(log2 K) qubits per stratum, so 40 qubits at K = 4, L = 20; the Hamiltonian encodes the same criterion by a different polynomial and raw energies are not compared
ballin-dirac3-native-energy-not-comparab: Section 6.1, p.18: no relation between the Dirac-3 native energy and the common QUBO energy is documented or established; the two are not compared directly, only through the common energy or the Bethel sample size
ballin-dirac3-mechanism-not-verified: Section 4.7, p.12: the authors state the physical mechanism was not independently verified and is reported as the provider describes it
ballin-dirac3-free-tier-100-variables-l2: Section 5.1, p.15: the 100-variable free-tier cap, the L x K variable count, the L = 25 ceiling 'under this reading', twenty strata (eighty variables) accepted, boundary not tested
ballin-dirac3-qudit-encoding-rejected: Section 4.7, p.11: the authors state they rejected an initial squared-difference label formulation because it imposes an artificial ordering and is minimised by a single cluster, and use the one-hot QUBO instead
ballin-surrogate-definition-dispersion-w: Section 4.1, p.6: the paper defines u_h, d_hh' and w_hh' = sqrt(N_h N_h') d_hh', and states the weighting is a design choice whose relation to the squared-distance identity is heuristic
ballin-surrogate-not-qubo-expressible-ra: Section 4.3, p.7 and Appendix A.3: the authors state that C_B(z) has no direct QUBO form and that dropping the 1/(2 N_k) factor changes the criterion and can alter partition ranking. A stated limit of their formulation, not a theorem
ballin-penalty-weight-below-sufficient-c: Section 4.2, pp.6-7: lambda = 3 max w = 476.92; the sufficient condition value is 1,729.23; the paper states the penalty used does not meet it and that decoded solutions were checked and repaired
ballin-repair-rule-all-feasible-four-str: Section 4.2, p.7: the repair rule is stated; energies and sample sizes are recomputed on the repaired partition; all Table 3 and Figure 5 results are stated as feasible with four non-empty strata
ballin-bethel-reported-is-ceiling-not-mi: Section 2, p.3: C_B reported = sum of component-wise ceilings, feasible but not guaranteed minimal; every method is scored by the same quantity
ballin-ga-evaluates-true-objective: Section 3, p.4: the paper describes the GA fitness as the Bethel-Chromy sample size at every evaluation, and shows the nested structure
ballin-amplify-control-not-same-penalise: Section 4.8, pp.12-13: the authors state the solver is not literally handed the same penalised polynomial and that a shortfall cannot rule out other algorithmic or computational limits
ballin-ai-tools-generated-code: Front matter, p.1: the AI-use statement and the reproducibility statement with the repository link are the paper's own disclosures
perceptron-qubit-encodes-sigmoid: Results, Quantum Perceptron, p.2: the paper defines the perceptron it studies as a qubit whose excitation probability encodes the sigmoid, via the gate in Eq. (1) taken from Ref. 34
ie-setup-numerical-parameters: Results, IE Performance, p.3: kappa = 2000, xmax = 12 and b_j = 0 are stated as the numerical setup
ie-success-distance-c-definition: Results p.3 defines C = 2 - F0 - F1 with F0, F1 as overlaps at the two ends; Quasi-optimal-time Solution p.4 sets C < 0.01 as the success criterion
ie-control-field-equations: Eqs. (6),(7) are derived in Methods (p.5) from the Schroedinger equation with the Eq. (5) parametrization: Eqs. (10),(11) are combined by adding and subtracting. Conditions (Hamiltonian Eq. 2, two Bloch angles) are in the paper. The derivation is short but shown
ie-control-independent-of-input: Results p.3: the paper states beta depends on x_j and that it fixes x_j = y, chosen to minimize C over an interval, to get one control field
faquad-constant-adiabatic-parameter: Methods, Fast Quasi-Adiabatic Method, pp.5-6: the paper states the FAQUAD protocol it implements keeps mu(t) = c, with the largest |mu| at |x_j/Omega_f| about 1.272 taken as the working condition
training-testing-copy-complexity-defined: Section 1.1, p.3: S and V are defined, and testing copy complexity is named as the requirement on V
three-learning-settings-states: Section 1.3, p.5: the three settings are defined in the paper; the unknown-mechanism case is reduced to S = 1
inductive-transductive-defined: Section 1.4, p.6: inductive and transductive learning are defined as the paper uses them
error-decomposition-and-new-contribution: Section 1.6.2, pp.10-11: excess testing error (Eq. 5) and knowledge gap (Eq. 6) are defined and the test-loss decomposition follows; the authors state their analysis is the main new contribution
uniform-deviation-bounds-can-be-loose: Section 1.8 p.14 and Section 2.2: the authors state that the uniform-deviation (Rademacher) bounds they use are worst-case over the class and can be loose
rademacher-limits-deep-nets: Section 2.2, p.20: the authors state that the capacity-based analysis leaves out the training algorithm and the data distribution, and that the bounds are vacuous when B(F) is much larger than N, as for deep networks
shadow-advantage-unclear: Section 4.2, p.32: the authors state it is unclear whether shadow tomography gives an exponential advantage for state discrimination. They state the open question about their own coverage
kernel-method-transductive-copies: Section 5.5, p.43: by the Section 1 definition, evaluating new kernels consumes further training copies, so the strategy is transductive; the paper states it
conclusion-three-error-terms: Section 7, p.48: the three-term decomposition is the one defined in Sections 1.6.1-1.6.2, and the authors state which method is best at exploiting training information is an open question
worst-case-formulation-used: Appendix D, p.55: the authors state they use the worst-case formulation, and that the optimal Bayesian measurement need not be inductive
corollary-a11-new: Corollary A.11, Appendix A, p.52: stated with its conditions (partition of X, functions constant on cells with p-norm at most B, lambda-Lipschitz margin loss) and proved in the paper by the contraction lemma, Cauchy-Schwarz and Jensen (A28-A31): R <= lambda B / sqrt(N) for p = 2 and lambda B / N times sum of sqrt(N_i) for p = infinity. The paper marks it new
copy-complexity-defined: Abstract, p.1, and Section 1.1: copy complexity is introduced and defined as the number of copies needed for a target accuracy
no-quantum-advantage-discussion: The new value matches Section 7, p.48: the two stated reasons and the pointer to future directions. The 'ad-hoc datasets' remark is the authors' stated reason, reported as such
cvqbm-single-visible-mode-scope: Section 2, p.4: the authors state they concentrate on a Hamiltonian that depends on a single visible qumode. The extension to several qumodes is only claimed as straightforward and is not shown
cvqbm-circuit-structure: Section 2, p.4: a visible and a hidden qumode, both in vacuum, entangled by U0; no further action on the hidden mode (Figs. 1, 2)
cvqbm-nonunitary-step-ancilla-projection: Section 2, p.6: each step T_s is Gaussian gates plus a projection of the ancilla onto n_A = 1 (Eq. 8). Note Section 5 later speaks of measuring 0 photons, an inconsistency in the paper that the value does not repeat
cvqbm-simulation-platform: Section 2, p.7: the CVQBM was simulated with Strawberry Fields and TensorFlow features
cvqbm-training-objective-fidelity-cost: Section 2, p.8: the cost is C = 1 - F with F defined in Eq. (14), and the Adam optimizer is stated
cvqbm-fock-cutoff: Section 2, p.8: the Fock-basis sum is truncated at a cutoff nmax in practice, as the paper states
cvqbm-kl-definition: Section 2, Eq. (18), p.8: the KL divergence is defined as the comparison metric, with value 0 when the distributions are equal (the paper spells it 'Kuller-Leibler')
cvqbm-sar-preprocessing-targets-are-fits: Section 3, pp.9-10: a 256-bin histogram, axis rescaling, and a SciPy Gaussian KDE to make the data continuous because discrete data needs a higher cutoff. Note the Fig. 3 and 4 captions call the target a fitted Gaussian or Weibull, which the value does not claim
cvqbm-standard-distributions-shared-setu: Section 3, p.12: S = 2, nmax = 15, 100 epochs, same Adam optimizer and schedule for the Rayleigh, Gamma and ET-IB cases
cvqbm-realistic-parameters-not-reached: Section 3, p.13 and Table 1: the Gamma parameters are close to real-world ones; Rayleigh and ET-IB are steeper and need a higher cutoff; the authors say real applications need HPC, better simulation or a CV quantum computer
cvqbm-quantum-training-settings: Section 4, p.15: cutoff 10 and Nelder-Mead for the CV QNN targets; Adam with a scheduler, learning rate 0.04, 400 epochs and cutoff 10 for the CVQBM
cvqbm-success-probability-product: Section 5, p.16: the post-selected success probability is defined as the product p1 p2 ... pS of the per-step probabilities, with the reason stated. The text says p_s is the chance of measuring 0 photons, while Section 2 projects onto 1 photon
cvqbm-photon-loss-mitigation-future: Section 5, p.18: the authors state that they leave photon loss mitigation to future work. The cited technique is reported as another paper's claim
cvqbm-hardware-limit: Section 5, p.16: the authors state the Xanadu X-series cannot accommodate their CVQBM mainly for lack of online squeezers; the new value names the device, as the passage does. A limit on realizing their own model
cvqbm-simulator-only: Section 1, p.3 and Section 5, p.16: the authors state that the experiments ran on a simulator and that hardware realization is left to future work
varemb-ansatz-definition: Eq. (2): the ansatz is defined as the product alpha_theta(sigma|eta) beta_delta(eta) with parameters {theta, delta}
varemb-global-variational: Introduction, p.1: the authors define 'variational and global' as optimizing the parameters of both models together
varemb-bath-only-sampling: Eqs. (5)-(6) and Appendix A, Eqs. (A3)-(A6): derived algebraically from the normalization condition sum over sigma of |alpha|^2 = 1 for all eta, so p_Psi = p_beta |alpha|^2 and the energy is a bath average of the weighted local energy. The condition is stated and the steps are in the paper
varemb-active-sum-exponential: Main text after Eq. (6), p.3: the authors state the sum over sigma scales exponentially in N_A, so it is feasible only for a small active partition
varemb-tractable-assumption: Appendix A, opening: the tractability assumption and its meaning are stated by the authors, citing [71]
varemb-hadamard-assumption: Appendix D: the authors assume different bath configurations give different circuits and say this is not true in general
varemb-parameter-shift: Appendix B part 1, Eq. (B5), p.12: the quantum gradient term uses the parameter shift rule extended to the Hadamard test, for the real and imaginary parts separately
varemb-tfim-setup: Transverse Field Ising, Eq. (10), p.3: a non-homogeneous TFIM chain with open boundaries; J_i > 1 in the active partition and J_i much smaller than 1 in the bath
varemb-ising-fixed-params: Transverse Field Ising, p.4, and Appendix E: 40 parameters for the hybrid model with three active spins; Jastrow 2N, RBM 2N + N^2, mean field 1
varemb-ising-reference-energies: Transverse Field Ising, p.4: E0 is exact up to 30 spins and from DMRG matrix product states beyond
varemb-ising-backflow-range: Appendix A part 2, p.9: the FFNN input is limited to a range of spins around the active partition, which fixes the parameter count independent of system size and allows more than 10^3 spins
varemb-ising-fig4-setup: Appendix A part 2, Fig. 4, p.9: 3 active spins (JA = 10), 8 bath spins (JB = 1e-2), Jint = 2; Jastrow 22 and RBM 143 parameters; mixed totals 54 and 84; exact optimization without sampling. The paper's split of 16 plus 8 plus 38 does not add to 54, but the value reports the stated totals
varemb-ising-2b-setup: Fig. 2 caption and Section on Transverse Field Ising: 10 bath and 3 active spins, ideal quantum simulator, error bars are classical sampling error only
varemb-ising-2b-couplings: Appendix E, p.13: JA = 1, JB = 0.25, Jint = 0.5 for panel (b), different from panel (a)
varemb-ising-2a-couplings: Appendix E, p.13: NA = 3, JA = 10, JB = 0.1, Jint = 0.1 for panel (a), with the stated reason for the choice
varemb-ammonia-setup: Molecular system, p.4, and Appendix F: NH3 in the IAO minimal basis from aug-cc-pVQZ, one N-H bond at 1.5 A, HONO/LUNO active space of four spin-orbitals, nitrogen 1s frozen
varemb-ammonia-simulator: Molecular system, p.4, and Appendix C: the quantum hardware part is evaluated on a classical simulator, with quantum overlaps evaluated exactly
varemb-ammonia-circuit: Molecular system, p.4: one double and two single excitation gates, 3 parameters
varemb-particle-preserving: Appendix A part 3, p.10: the RBM is restricted to physical configurations, the sample-to-angle function outputs missing electrons, and the circuit uses single and double excitation gates
varemb-optimizer-classical: Appendix C, p.12: xi = 0.001, shift 0.001, 5000 iterations up to 500 spins and 2500 above, 10^3 samples
varemb-optimizer-quantum: Appendix C, p.12: xi between 0.005 and 0.01, regularization 0.001, ADAM at 0.01 for the sample-to-angle network and circuit, 10^4 samples
varemb-vqe-simulator: Appendix F part 1, p.14: VQE runs use a classical simulator without shots and noise
varemb-partition-open: Discussion, p.5: the authors name optimal partitioning and other network architectures as open directions, so their method does not address them
varemb-noise-not-studied: Discussion, p.5: the authors state hardware noise effects should be investigated, so they were not studied; the Fig. 2 caption and Appendices C and F confirm noiseless simulation

theory_low.generalization-bound-small-input-space: Section 1.7, p.13: bound (14) is stated as approximate, with conditions in the garbled formula; the proof sits in Section 5.3 and Appendix B and is not in the quotes. The conditions are not in the quotes
theory_low.tomography-impractical-large-dimension: Section 1.7, p.13: the impracticality is the authors' interpretation of the O(d/sqrt(NS)) scaling, which rests on the cited tomography copy count [81] (Section 4.2). Not settled by this paper alone
theory_low.transductive-knowledge-gap-dimension-fre: Section 1.7, p.13: an overview claim, O((NS)^-1/3) with logarithmic factors ignored. The derivation uses state exponentiation from cited work [36, 37] with an approximation assumption (Sections 4.5, 5.2); not a stated and proved theorem
theory_low.both-errors-vanish-large-N-fixed-S: Section 1.7, p.13: argued in prose from the learner seeing infinitely many copies. No theorem or proof
theory_low.constraints-reduce-generalization-error-: Section 1.8, p.14: argued in prose from the data processing inequality; the words 'generally' and 'expected' show it is not a proved result
theory_low.locality-sample-bound: Section 1.8, p.15: derived from a mutual-information bound with an approximate sign (N is about O(2^k)). It also needs I(Y:Q_N) close to I(Y:Q), a condition the quote drops and the text states loosely
theory_low.fourier-frequencies-more-data: Section 1.9.1, p.16: an upper bound (23) is read as 'more data are required'. An upper bound cannot show a requirement. The derivation is in Appendix C and relies on the model of cited work [44]
theory_low.phase-classification-local-order-paramet: Section 1.9.2, p.16: the text says 'we expect'; it is an expectation, supported by a numerical experiment in a cited reference [8], and global orders are called open
theory_low.entanglement-classification-exponential-: Section 1.9.3, p.17: derived from an upper bound in a toy problem. An upper bound alone does not show that the sample count must grow exponentially. No proof is given in the quotes
theory_low.optimal-measurement-nonlocal: Section 3.3, p.25: the second half, that simpler adaptive strategies are only known to be optimal for pure states, is cited from [74]. The non-locality of the Helstrom measurement is a known property, not a limit of this paper's own work
theory_low.majority-rule-perfect-discrimination: Section 3.3, p.26: argued with a large-V approximation of the binomial tail and a KL term, not a numbered theorem. It is the authors' prose conclusion
theory_low.optimal-error-exponential-in-copies: Section 3.3, pp.25-26: the exponential decay follows from the Fuchs-van de Graaf inequalities and the Helstrom form, which are cited. The suboptimal-exponent remark is not proved
theory_low.fidelity-classifier-pure-states: Section 3.4.4, p.29: the fidelity classifier is named after cited work [36] and holds for pure states under a hinge loss with a Hilbert-Schmidt penalty. The conditions are dropped from the value. The shot count remark is heuristic
theory_low.empirical-helstrom-can-be-worst: Section 4.2, p.31: an argument with an example ('could be'), not a theorem with conditions. It is a plausible remark, not a proved result
theory_low.fixed-measurement-rademacher-entropy: Section 4.3, pp.32-33: the bound (87) uses Theorem A.9, credited to Blanchard and cited, plus Jensen's inequality. The 'fewer outcomes are preferable' reading is an interpretation of an upper bound
theory_low.helstrom-transductive-copies-dimension-f: Section 4.5, pp.34-35: S = O(-log(eps) eps^-3) is a derivation that assumes each unitary has the same error and builds on cited state exponentiation [36, 37]. Not a formal theorem
theory_low.representer-strategy-fewer-copies-when-c: Section 4.6, p.36: compares two upper bounds for pure states and says 'is expected'. Not a proved result
theory_low.transductive-worse-in-V-than-inductive: Section 4.7, p.36: argued by splitting the training set among V test states; the size of the effect is not given. A prose argument
theory_low.transductive-exponential-advantage-in-n: Section 4.7, p.37: hedged with 'may', and compares two upper bounds. Not a proved separation
theory_low.majority-rule-generalization-grows-slowl: Section 5.1.1, p.39 and Appendix B part 3: the authors call it a proof of a conjecture, but the qualitative 'only slightly increases' rests on bound (104), garbled in the text layer, and the training-error decay is from the Section 3.3 approximation. The conditions are not in the quotes
theory_low.copy-and-data-tradeoff-extremes: Section 5.2, pp.39-40: argued in prose for the two extremes S to infinity and S = 1. No theorem
theory_low.tomography-S-vs-N-tradeoff: Section 5.2, p.40: follows from the tomography scaling cited from [81] (epsilon = O(d/sqrt(NS))) and the Rademacher bound; it is a scaling remark, not a stated and proved theorem
theory_low.helstrom-S-must-grow-with-N: Section 5.2, p.40: a scaling argument combining the state exponentiation gap (cited methods) and the generalization bound, in big-O terms with logarithmic corrections. Not a proved result
theory_low.generalization-with-imperfect-copies: Section 5.3.1, p.42: follows from bound (110), garbled in the text layer; the conditions on the environment model are not in the quotes
theory_low.observable-norm-bounds-exponential-qubit: Section 5.4, p.42: a remark on bound (113) applied to Pauli sums, from Appendix B part 4. The bound itself is garbled in the quotes and the conditions are not carried
theory_low.infinity-norm-observables-equal-povm-bou: Section 5.4, p.42: asserted by comparing bound (113) with (109); the comparison is a one-line statement and the bounds are garbled in the text layer, so the conditions are not in the quotes
theory_low.kernel-error-scaling-distinguishability: Section 5.5, p.43: a lower bound from Jensen's inequality and a divergent prefactor; not a full analysis of the kernel loss, and the condition rho_S+ close to rho_S- is loose
theory_low.capacity-bounds-fail-overparameterized: Section 5.6, p.45: this is a statement about the cited bounds of Caro et al. and Du et al., and about overparameterized QNNs, which is a field claim. It is not a limit of this paper's own work
theory_low.generative-excess-risk-open: Section 6.3, p.47: the open-problem remark is the authors' view, and the claim that very few works study generative generalization is a field statement the paper does not show
theory_low.cvqbm-output-as-thermal-state: Section 2, Eqs. (10)-(11), p.7: a short argument, with no theorem or conditions. Any positive operator can be written as exp(-H_eff), so 'can be viewed as a thermal state' is an interpretation
theory_low.cvqbm-quantum-gadget-fidelity-estimator: Section 4, Eqs. (24)-(27), pp.13-14: P1 - P0 = |<Phi|Psi>|^2 is shown with steps but without stated conditions (ideal CSWAP), and the Kerr-gate implementation of the CSWAP is cited from [30, 31]. The value mixes a cited claim with the identity

requote.erm-generally-inapplicable-quantum-data: regraded LOW at the team lead's decision: Abstract p.1 and Section 1.1: the authors argue in prose that measurement disturbance prevents evaluating the training loss on several hypotheses with the same data. It is a general claim about quantum learning with no theorem or proof, and not a scope statement. The passage lacks a formal statement or a stated condition set
